newsitem.title: UK: Facia heads for liquidation - paper.
newsitem.headline: Facia heads for liquidation - paper.

text.p: Facia, the privately-owned British retailer which collapsed in June, is set to go into liquidation shortly with the appointment of accountants Stoy Hayward, the Independent on Sunday newspaper said.

The payout for Facia's ordinary creditors was expected to be at the top end of the 700,000 stg ($1.12 million) to 5.6 million stg range indicated in August, after better-than-expected recovery of assets by receivers KPMG and Grant Thornton.
Stoy Hayward was said to be the choice of retail group Sears for the liquidation of all the Facia companies, against which it has lodged a 30 million stg claim.

Facia, which owned such stores as Sock Shop and Saxone, was run by British entrepreneur Stephen Hinchliffe. Britain's Department of Trade and Industry is seeking to ban him as a company director for his involvement in another collapsed firm.
No-one at receivers KPMG was immediately available for comment.
